title: Hercules, Iolaus and the Hydra
text:
The second labor that King Eurystheus set for Heracles was to kill the Hydra, a monstrous serpent living in the swamps of Lerna. According to the mythographer Apollodorus, it had nine heads, and the middle one could not die.

Heracles drove to Lerna in a chariot with his nephew Iolaus at the reins. He forced the Hydra out of its lair with burning arrows and grappled with it. But every time he smashed one of its heads with his club, two new ones grew in its place. To make things worse, a giant crab came out of the swamp to help the Hydra and bit him on the foot. He killed the crab, but he was making no progress against the monster.

So Heracles called to Iolaus for help. Iolaus set fire to part of a nearby wood, and each time Heracles cut off a head, Iolaus seared the stump with a burning branch so that no new heads could sprout. Working together, they destroyed the heads one after another. At last Heracles cut off the immortal head, buried it under a heavy rock, and dipped his arrows in the Hydra's poisonous gall.

Eurystheus later refused to count this labor, because Heracles had not done it alone.
lesson: Some problems multiply faster than one person can handle them and need a partner who deals with what you cannot. Do not let anyone shame you for having had help.
date: Ancient Greek myth; text 1st or 2nd century AD
